# Hazel of Borrowing Base (`hazel-of-borrowing-base`)

Prepares a nursing-home borrowing base certificate from aged receivables: eligible receivables by payer type, ineligibles by reason (over age, cross-aged, Medicaid pending, credit balances, payer concentration), availability at your advance rates and the room left on the line. Arithmetic on your loan terms. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Hazel never signs or sends a certificate to a lender. Hazel never draws on the line.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y hazel-of-borrowing-base demo
npx -y hazel-of-borrowing-base mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow receivables for a 31 March 2026 certificate, with a 300000 line and 240000 drawn. Planted:

- R1603: Medicare from October, over the 120-day limit.
- R1606: Medicaid pending, never eligible.
- R1609: private pay with most of the balance over 90 days, so the current 6200 is cross-aged out too.
- R1611: a private pay credit of 1300 comes off eligible receivables.
- Sunrise Advantage is 29% of eligible receivables, so the excess over 25% is out.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a term, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `hazel_check` | Work out eligible receivables, ineligibles by reason and availability for the certificate. | runs |
| `hazel_write_report` | Write hazel-borrowing-base.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and hazel-borrowing-base.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/hazel). | runs |
| `hazel_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `hazel_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `hazel_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `hazel_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `certificate_submit` | Hazel never signs or sends a certificate to a lender. | refused |
| `line_draw` | Hazel never draws on the line. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `hazel_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `ar` (required) | Aged receivables by resident under --root: resident, payer, payer type, service or invoice date, balance |
| `terms` | Loan terms JSON: advance rates, age limits, cross-aging, concentration, ineligible payer types, line limit, loan balance |
| `as_of` | Certificate date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx hazel-of-borrowing-base inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Aged receivables (`ar`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `service_date` | date | Service Date, Service To, Through, Invoice Date, DOS, Bill Date |
| `balance` (required) | amount | Balance, Open Balance, Outstanding, Amount |

## Settings file (`hazel_terms`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `advance_rates` | Advance rate by payer type, from your loan agreement |
| `max_age_days` | Age limit in days by payer type, plus default |
| `cross_age_pct` | Cross-aging percent (default 50) |
| `concentration_pct` | Most one managed care or commercial payer may be of eligible receivables, percent (default 25) |
| `ineligible_types` | Payer types that are never eligible |
| `line_limit` | Line of credit commitment |
| `outstanding` | Loan balance today |

## Memory

`hazel_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `hazel_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `lender_note` | is shown with results. It never changes the base. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hazel-of-borrowing-base": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "hazel-of-borrowing-base",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add hazel-of-borrowing-base -- npx -y hazel-of-borrowing-base mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
hazel-of-borrowing-base tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
hazel-of-borrowing-base sources               # the columns each input is read from
hazel-of-borrowing-base inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
hazel-of-borrowing-base call hazel_check '{"ar":"<ar>"}'
hazel-of-borrowing-base eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
hazel-of-borrowing-base demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
